reasons.plausibility: Increasing cooling rate is a well-known method to promote amorphization, but the hypothesis incorrectly claims it will also enhance thermal stability; faster cooling typically produces a more loosely packed, less stable glass with lower crystallization onset temperature, contradicting established understanding.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on DSC and XRD measurements comparing high and standard cooling rate samples.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is based on a physically incorrect premise regarding thermal stability, and testing it would not advance understanding of how to improve both glass-forming ability and stability in this alloy system.
